results.project_title: Early Life Adversity and Affective Dynamics: Integrating EMA And Multimodal MRI To Understand Depression Risk
results.phr_text:
Project Narrative
Early life adversity has been linked to greater depression, but the mechanisms mediating these linkages are
still unclear. Here, we explore an understudied, potential pathway-- brain and behavioral responses to positive
affect. Understanding such connections could aid in improving mental health in those exposed to adversity.

results.project_title: Investigating Links Between Racial and Ethnic Discrimination, Neurobiology, and Internalizing Symptomatology
results.phr_text:
Project Narrative:
Racial and ethnic discrimination are linked to greater depression and anxiety in African-
American and Latino/a youth. This may be due to brain connectivity changes, potentially for
emotion- and reward-related brain areas. Understanding these linkages could aid in improving
mental health and well-being in communities of Color.

results.project_title: Neurodevelopmental Pathways Linking Physical Abuse and Affective Dysregulation
results.phr_text:
Project Narrative
Physical abuse can create risk for later depression or anxiety; however, why this occurs is
poorly understood. Here, we will study the effect of abuse on emotion-related brain circuitry.
Information from this proposed work could increase our understanding of the affective
dysregulation seen after early adversity.
